name: jq
plain: `jq` is like sed and awk for JSON. JSON is the text format almost every web API and many tools (nmap -oJ, tshark, docker inspect, BloodHound, cloud CLIs) speak. jq pretty-prints it, picks out fields, filters lists and reshapes them.
You give it a filter, a small expression such as `.name` (the name field) or `.[] | select(.port == 80)` (items whose port is 80).
when: Read a big JSON response comfortably.
Extract one field from an API reply.
Filter a list by a condition.
Turn JSON into plain lines or CSV for other tools.
Process tool output (tshark -T json, docker inspect, ffuf -of json).

examples.title: Pretty-print
examples.explain: The dot means 'the whole input'. jq indents and colours it.

examples.title: Raw text, no quotes
examples.explain: -r prints strings without the surrounding quotes, so you can use them in the shell.

examples.title: Every item of a list
examples.explain: .[] walks through the list; | passes each item to the next filter.

examples.title: Filter
examples.explain: select keeps only items where the test is true.

examples.title: Build a new object
examples.explain: Curly braces create a new object with just the fields you want.

examples.title: To CSV
examples.explain: @csv, @tsv, @base64, @uri and @sh format values; here each item becomes a CSV row.

examples.title: Count
examples.explain: length of a list or object.

examples.title: Compact one-line output
examples.explain: -c puts each result on one line, which suits grep and wc -l.

examples.title: Decode a base64 field
examples.explain: @base64d decodes base64 text inside the pipeline.

examples.title: Pass a variable in
examples.explain: --arg safely passes a shell value into the filter.

options.plain: The program: ., .key, .[], .[0], |, select(), map(), keys, length, ...
Like -r with no newline between outputs.
Read all inputs into one array.
Do not read any input; start from null.
Set the exit code from the last output (false/null gives 1).
Treat each input line as a string.
Read the filter from a file.
Load a file into a variable.
Treat remaining arguments as positional strings / JSON.
Use tabs or N spaces for indentation.
Use the application/json-seq format / stream large inputs.

mistakes: Quoting: always wrap the filter in single quotes so the shell leaves $ and | alone.
Forgetting -r and getting values with quotes.
Using .[] on an object (it iterates the values, not the keys): use keys or to_entries.
Expecting jq to accept invalid JSON: remove prefixes or comments first.
Using --arg for numbers (it is a string): use --argjson.
try: Save an API reply and list every key with jq 'keys'.
Filter a list to items with a condition using select.
Turn a list of objects into CSV with @csv.
